mainTopic: Posture during קריאת שמע, the exemption of one busy with a מצוה, the status of acting like בית שמאי, and the ברכות of קריאת שמע
overview: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי reject בית הלל's reading. They answer that if the תורה meant only times, it would have said 'morning and evening.' Since it says 'when you lie down and when you rise,' it means actual lying down and actual standing. בית שמאי use ובלכתך בדרך for a ברייתא that exempts a חתן and anyone busy with a מצוה. This leads to a discussion that ends with the rule that only טרדא דמצוה, distraction caused by a מצוה, exempts from קריאת שמע. A ברייתא and a story about רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה show that the הלכה follows בית הלל: any posture is fine. Three אמוראים then argue about someone who acted like בית שמאי. רב יחזקאל says it counts, רב יוסף says it counts for nothing, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says he deserves death. A new משנה lists the ברכות before and after שמע and says their set form may not be changed. The גמרא begins asking what the first ברכה says, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why don't בית שמאי agree with בית הלל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that בית הלל explained both sides' verses, and asks what בית שמאי's reason is for not following בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It makes sense for בית הלל, since they explain their own reason and also the reason of בית שמאי. But בית שמאי, why don't they say like בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking what בית שמאי's reasoning is. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives בית שמאי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל gave a full picture. They used ובלכתך בדרך to show that everyone may read שמע in any position, and they explained בשכבך ובקומך as describing the time when people go to sleep and wake up. בית שמאי only quoted their own verse, so the גמרא wants to know why they reject בית הלל's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
It makes sense / granted (introduces the side that is easy to understand)

phrases.english: GEMARA
Granted, Beit Hillel:
they explain their own reason
phrases.notes: Their verse: ובלכתך בדרך

phrases.english: and also the reason of Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: They explain away בשכבך ובקומך as meaning 'at the time people lie down and rise'

phrases.english: but Beit Shammai:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי כְּבֵית הִלֵּל?
phrases.english: what is the reason they do not say like Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל קָא מְפָרְשִׁי טַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's מחלוקת about posture during קריאת שמע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What textual reason do בית שמאי have for rejecting בית הלל's reading of בשכבך ובקומך as a time indicator?

steps.title: בית שמאי: the verse would have said 'morning and evening'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that if the verse were only giving times, it would say 'morning and evening.' The wording 'lying down' and 'rising' means actual posture.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי could say to you: If so, let the verse say 'in the morning and in the evening.' Why does it say 'when you lie down and when you rise'? To teach that at the time of lying down, one must actually be lying down, and at the time of rising, one must actually be standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's reason, which is based on the exact wording of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about unnecessary wording. The תורה had a simpler way to state a time ('morning and evening'). By choosing words that describe the body's position, it must be telling us something about posture. So בית שמאי hold that the verse teaches both the time and the position.
steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי do not ignore the time element. They agree the verse refers to the times of night and morning. They add that at those times, one's body must actually be in that position.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai could say to you:
If so, let the verse say
"in the morning and in the evening",
what is meant by "when you lie down and when you rise"?
At the time of lying down, actual lying down,
and at the time of rising, actual rising.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: אִם כֵּן, נֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse's choice of posture words instead of 'morning and evening' shows that it requires actual lying down at night and actual standing in the morning.

steps.title: What do בית שמאי do with 'when you walk on the way'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בית שמאי handle the phrase ובלכתך בדרך, which בית הלל used to show that one reads שמע in whatever position he is in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, what do they do with this phrase, 'and when you walk on the way'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the other side: בית הלל's proof verse. It wants to know how בית שמאי use it. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל argued that ובלכתך בדרך shows a person reads שמע however he happens to be, even while walking. If בית שמאי reject that, the phrase seems to have no purpose in their view. The גמרא assumes every phrase in the תורה must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: And when you walk on the way

keyTerms.term: מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ / מַאי עֲבִיד לְהוּ
keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (How do they use this verse?)

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai:
this phrase "and when you walk on the way",
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי הַאי וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ מַאי עֲבִיד לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining בית שמאי's verse, the גמרא turns to בית הלל's verse and asks how בית שמאי use it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the phrase ובלכתך בדרך teach according to בית שמאי, since they do not use it to permit any posture?

steps.title: The verse exempts one busy with a מצוה and a חתן
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי use the verse for a ברייתא: בשבתך בביתך excludes someone busy with a מצוה, and ובלכתך בדרך excludes a חתן. From this: one who marries a בתולה is exempt, but one who marries an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need that phrase for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'When you sit in your house' excludes one who is busy with a מצוה. 'And when you walk on the way' excludes a groom. From here they said: One who marries a virgin is exempt, but one who marries a widow is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי need ובלכתך בדרך for a different law, taught in a ברייתא, about who is exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting at home and walking on the road are a person's own optional activities. So the obligation applies during ordinary activity, and someone busy with a מצוה is exempt. A חתן who marries a בתולה is anxious and preoccupied with his מצוה, so he is exempt. One who marries an אלמנה is not as preoccupied, so he must still read. The גמרא will next explain exactly how these exemptions come out of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
One who is busy performing a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי read בשכבך ובקומך as requiring actual posture, since otherwise the verse would say 'morning and evening.' They use ובלכתך בדרך for the ברייתא exempting one busy with a מצוה and a חתן who marries a בתולה, but not one who marries an אלמנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה, that one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another, is a major halachic rule throughout ש״ס. This ברייתא is a key source for it.

phrases.english: That phrase is needed by them,
for what was taught in a baraita:
"When you sit in your house":
excluding one who is busy with a מצוה,
"and when you walk on the way":
excluding a groom.
From here they said:
One who marries a virgin is exempt,
phrases.notes: He is preoccupied with his מצוה on the wedding night

phrases.english: but one who marries a widow is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by assigning ובלכתך בדרך a different purpose for בית שמאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי use ובלכתך בדרך (with בשבתך בביתך) to exempt one busy with a מצוה and a חתן from קריאת שמע. This yields the rule that one marrying a בתולה is exempt, while one marrying an אלמנה is obligated.

steps.title: How does the verse show that a groom is exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words ובלכתך בדרך teach that a חתן is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind the ברייתא from the last step. How do the words 'when you walk on the way' show that a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא linked ובלכתך בדרך to exempting a חתן, but the connection is not obvious. Nothing in the phrase mentions a groom or a מצוה. The גמרא wants to see the reasoning that gets us from the verse to the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the implication? / How is this derived?
And when you walk on the way (from the verse of שמע)

phrases.english: What is the implication? (How is this derived?)
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא's use of ובלכתך בדרך to exempt a חתן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the derivation behind the ברייתא quoted in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase ובלכתך בדרך implies an exemption for a חתן.

steps.title: רב פפא: just as travel is voluntary, so too everything else
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא compares all activities to the 'way': the obligation applies only to voluntary activity, like ordinary travel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is like 'the way.' Just as a journey is a voluntary activity, so too all the situations meant here are voluntary.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that 'the way' is the model. A normal trip is a personal, optional activity, so the verse obligates you only when you are doing optional things. Someone busy with a מצוה, like a חתן, is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a comparison: the verse's example, travel, sets the type of activity it is talking about. Since travel is רשות (optional), the obligation is limited to optional activities. A מצוה activity falls outside that and is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first explanation
Like 'the way': comparing to the journey in the verse
Just as... so too: a comparison formula

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Like 'the way.'
Just as a journey is voluntary,
so too all cases are voluntary.
phrases.notes: So the obligation applies only to voluntary activity. מצוה activity is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי דֶרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'way' in the verse is a voluntary activity, so the verse obligates only during voluntary activities. Those busy with a מצוה are exempt.

steps.title: But a journey can also be for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the verse also covers someone traveling for a מצוה, yet still obligates him, so 'way' does not mean only voluntary travel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Aren't we also dealing with someone who is traveling for a מצוה? And even so, the תורה said he should recite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. The verse never says the trip is optional. It could be a trip for a מצוה, and the Torah still says to read שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's comparison assumed that 'the way' always means optional travel. The גמרא points out that the verse is general, so it includes מצוה trips too. If so, the verse actually obligates even someone doing a מצוה, which is the opposite of what we wanted to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with...? (a challenge formula)
A purpose that is a מצוה

phrases.english: Are we not dealing with
a case where he is going for a מצוה,
and even so the Torah said: let him recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָא אָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's comparison from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that 'the way' means only voluntary travel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is general and includes trips for a מצוה, which are still obligated. So the comparison cannot prove an exemption for מצוה activity.

steps.title: The proof comes from the word 'your'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the exemption from the extra word 'your' instead. The Torah could have written 'when sitting and when walking.' 'Your sitting' and 'your walking' means your own activities, not מצוה activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the תורה write 'when sitting and when walking.' Why does it say 'when you sit and when you walk'? It means: in your own sitting and your own walking you are obligated, but in a מצוה's sitting or walking you are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new proof that replaces the 'way' comparison. The extra word 'your' (בשבתך, בלכתך) limits the obligation to your personal activities. When you are doing something for a מצוה, you are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah meant to obligate in every case, a plain 'when sitting and walking' would have been enough. The extra 'your' must teach something: activities done for your own purposes. That excludes מצוה activities like a חתן's, which are done for ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: When sitting and when walking (wording without 'your')

steps.whatToRemember: The rule עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה (one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה) is learned here from the extra word 'your' in בשבתך and בלכתך.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא's 'way' comparison still stands. It was rejected in Step 7. The working proof is the word 'your.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source in the גמרא for the principle that someone busy with one מצוה is exempt from another.

phrases.english: If so, let the Torah write
'when sitting and when walking.'
Why 'when you sit and when you walk'?
In your own sitting and your own walking
you are obligated,
but in that of a מצוה you are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּשֶׁבֶת וּבְלֶכֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב פפא's comparison, gives a new derivation for the question of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New textual derivation from extra wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is general and obligates even someone traveling for a מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'your' limits the obligation to personal activities, so someone busy with a מצוה is exempt.

steps.title: Then even one who marries a widow should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: If every מצוה activity exempts, then one who marries an אלמנה should also be exempt. That contradicts the ברייתא, which obligates him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even one who marries a widow should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the new rule further and finds a problem. Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה, so he should be exempt too. But the ברייתא said he is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 8 is broad: anyone doing a מצוה is exempt. The ברייתא, however, splits the cases: one who marries a בתולה is exempt, but one who marries an אלמנה is obligated. The גמרא needs to explain why one is exempt and the other is not. Step 10 answers this.

phrases.english: If so,
even one who marries a widow should also be exempt?
phrases.notes: This contradicts the ברייתא in Step 4, which obligates him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ כּוֹנֵס אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad rule set up in Step 8 by comparing it with the ברייתא's ruling in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that anyone busy with a מצוה is exempt from קריאת שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה, so the rule would exempt him. Yet the ברייתא says he is obligated.

steps.title: The groom of a virgin is preoccupied, the groom of a widow is not
steps.stepSummary: The difference between marrying a בתולה and marrying an אלמנה is preoccupation. The first groom is anxious and distracted. The second is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (who marries a virgin) is preoccupied, and that one (who marries a widow) is not preoccupied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. A חתן who marries a בתולה is worried and distracted, so he is exempt. A man who marries an אלמנה is not distracted, so he must still say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is not just because 'he is busy with a מצוה.' The real reason is that he is mentally distracted (טרוד) and cannot concentrate. The groom of a בתולה worries that he may find she is not a בתולה, while the groom of an אלמנה has no such worry. This fits the ברייתא that obligates the man who marries an אלמנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the exemption depends only on doing a מצוה. From here on, the key factor is the groom's state of mind, his distraction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of טרדא (preoccupation) as the real basis of the חתן's exemption. The rest of this passage builds on that idea.

phrases.english: This one is preoccupied,
phrases.notes: The man marrying a virgin, who worries whether she is truly a virgin.

phrases.english: and that one is not preoccupied.
phrases.notes: The man marrying a widow, who has no such worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי טְרִיד, וְהַאי לָא טְרִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 9 about the man who marries an אלמנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the reason for the exemption: mental preoccupation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any מצוה activity, including marrying an אלמנה, should exempt a person from שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a person who is actually distracted, like the groom of a בתולה, is exempt.

steps.title: Then someone whose ship sank should also be exempt
steps.stepSummary: If distraction is the reason for the exemption, then anyone very distracted should be exempt. That would include a person whose ship just sank.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of preoccupation, then even one whose ship sank at sea should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 10. If distraction exempts a person, then someone who just lost his ship at sea should also be exempt from שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 made distraction the key factor. The problem is that distraction is everywhere: anyone with a big loss or worry is distracted. The גמרא is testing whether that rule is too broad.

phrases.english: If it is because of preoccupation,
then even one whose ship sank at sea should also be exempt!
phrases.notes: Someone who suffered a great financial loss is surely distracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם טִרְדָּא, אֲפִילּוּ טָבְעָה סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in Step 10 by stretching it to an extreme case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 10 that טרדא is what exempts the חתן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If distraction exempts, then every distracted person should be exempt, such as one whose ship sank. That seems wrong.

steps.title: Proof that preoccupation alone does not exempt: the mourner
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that the ship-loser really is exempt. The גמרא blocks that answer with רב's ruling: an אבל is obligated in all מצוות except תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that indeed he is exempt, why then did רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: A mourner is obligated in all the commandments stated in the Torah except תפילין, since 'splendor' is said about them, as it says: 'Bind your splendor upon yourself'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible escape from its question. Someone might say the ship-loser really is exempt. But רב rules that even an אבל, who is deeply pained and distracted, must keep all מצוות, including שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is surely at least as distracted as someone who lost money, yet he is still obligated. His only exemption is from תפילין, and that is for a different reason: תפילין are called 'splendor' (פאר), which does not fit a mourner. So distraction by itself does not exempt a person, and the question against Step 10 becomes even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא heads off a possible answer)
Splendor, glory (the word used for תפילין)

steps.confusionAlert: The אבל's exemption from תפילין is NOT because he is distracted. It is because תפילין are 'splendor,' which is not fitting for a mourner. That is exactly why this ruling proves that distraction alone does not exempt anyone.

phrases.english: And if you say: indeed, he is also exempt,

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: why then did Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say that Rav said:
A mourner is obligated in all the commandments
stated in the Torah,
except for tefillin,
since 'splendor' is said about them,
as it says: 'Bind your splendor upon yourself' (Ezekiel 24:17)?!
phrases.notes: Said to יחזקאל when he was told not to mourn. This implies a regular mourner would not wear his 'splendor,' meaning תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי, אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of Step 11 by ruling out the answer 'yes, he is exempt.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that anyone distracted, even the ship-loser, is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אבל is very distracted, yet רב obligates him in every מצוה except תפילין. So distraction alone does not exempt a person, and the חתן's exemption still needs an explanation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבא בר זבדא in the name of רב, based on יחזקאל 24:17

steps.title: Distraction from a מצוה exempts; ordinary distraction does not
steps.stepSummary: The חתן's distraction comes from a מצוה, so it exempts him. A loss like a sunken ship causes ordinary, non-מצוה distraction, which does not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he is preoccupied with a מצוה preoccupation. Here, he is preoccupied with a voluntary (non-מצוה) preoccupation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Only distraction that comes from doing a מצוה exempts a person. The חתן's worry is tied to his מצוה of marriage, while the ship-loser's worry is a private, everyday matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two earlier ideas now combine. Doing a מצוה alone is not enough, as the groom of an אלמנה shows. Distraction alone is not enough either, as the ship-loser and the אבל show. Only distraction that comes from a מצוה (טרדא דמצוה) exempts from קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Preoccupation that comes from a מצוה
Preoccupation from a voluntary, non-מצוה matter

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן who marries a בתולה is exempt from קריאת שמע because of two things together: he is busy with a מצוה, and that מצוה makes him truly distracted. Ordinary distraction, even from a great loss or from mourning, does not exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הָתָם' (there) means the חתן and 'הָכָא' (here) means the ship-loser. It does not refer to the אבל from the last step.

phrases.english: There, he is preoccupied with the preoccupation of a מצוה,
phrases.notes: The חתן, whose worry comes from his מצוה of marriage.

phrases.english: here, he is preoccupied with the preoccupation of a voluntary matter.
phrases.notes: The one whose ship sank. His worry is a personal, non-מצוה matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם טְרִיד טִרְדָּא דְמִצְוָה, הָכָא טְרִיד טִרְדָּא דִרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Steps 11 and 12 by narrowing what kind of distraction exempts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: מצוה-based preoccupation versus voluntary preoccupation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any distraction, even from a lost ship, should exempt from שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only טרדא דמצוה exempts. Distraction from personal matters, like loss or mourning, does not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חתן's exemption requires both a מצוה and real distraction caused by that מצוה.

steps.title: How do בית שמאי read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its earlier question: what do בית שמאי learn from 'ובלכתך בדרך'? They do not use it, as בית הלל do, to show that one may recite in any position.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא now turns back to ask how בית שמאי use the words 'ובלכתך בדרך,' and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the long side discussion about the חתן and טרדא (steps 5–13), the גמרא comes back to the question of step 3. בית הלל use 'ובלכתך בדרך' to show that one recites in whatever position he is in. בית שמאי reject that reading, so what does the phrase teach them? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And בית שמאי (how do they explain it)?
The school of שמאי, who disagree with בית הלל about how to recite שמע

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai? (How do they explain 'when you walk along the way'?)
phrases.notes: Two-word question that returns to the earlier question of step 3.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the טרדא discussion, the גמרא returns to the opinion of בית שמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How בית שמאי interpret 'ובלכתך בדרך,' given their view about how to recite שמע.

steps.title: בית שמאי use the verse to exempt someone on a מצוה mission
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי need 'ובלכתך בדרך' to exclude שלוחי מצוה from the obligation of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed by them to exclude people who are on the way to do a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14: what do בית שמאי learn from 'ובלכתך בדרך'? They learn that someone traveling for a מצוה is exempt from שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי already read 'בשכבך ובקומך' as being about body position. So they still have 'ובלכתך בדרך' free to teach something else. They read it as 'when you walk on YOUR way', meaning your own private business. That excludes someone whose trip is for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (the verse is needed for a different teaching)
People on a mission to do a מצוה

phrases.english: That [verse] they need it
phrases.notes: 'They' = בית שמאי

phrases.english: to exclude those who are on a מצוה mission.
phrases.notes: Links back to the חתן discussion: busy with a מצוה = exempt

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבְּעֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What בית שמאי learn from 'ובלכתך בדרך'.

steps.title: בית הלל learn by implication that a traveler does recite שמע
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל also use the verse for the מצוה-mission exemption. As a side result, it shows that an ordinary traveler recites שמע on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: automatically, learn from it that even on the road one also recites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא deals with an unspoken problem. If בית הלל also use this verse for the שלוחי מצוה exemption, where do they get the rule that one may say שמע while walking? The answer is that this rule comes out of the same verse automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse exempts only someone traveling for a מצוה. That means a person on an ordinary trip is still obligated, and he says שמע even while on the road. So one verse teaches both points, and בית הלל need no extra source.
steps.confusionAlert: The question this answers is not written in our text. It is implied: 'But בית הלל also need the verse for שלוחי מצוה, so where do they learn that one may recite while walking?' The line we have is only the answer.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
By implication, learn from it
phrases.notes: From the exemption of the מצוה traveler

phrases.english: that even on the road one also recites.
phrases.notes: An ordinary traveler is obligated and recites while walking

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אָמְרִי: מִמֵּילָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an implied challenge that arises once step 15 assigns the verse to שלוחי מצוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Double use of one verse (explicit exclusion plus implied rule)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If בית הלל use the verse for שלוחי מצוה, they would have no source for reciting while walking.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exclusion itself implies that a regular traveler recites on the road.

steps.title: ברייתא: בית הלל allow שמע in any position
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the positions in which בית הלל permit reciting שמע: standing, sitting, reclining, walking, even working.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בית הלל say: people stand and recite, sit and recite, recline and recite, walk on the road and recite, do their work and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out בית הלל's view in full. Body position does not matter at all for שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי tie the evening שמע to lying down and the morning שמע to standing. בית הלל say any posture works, even in the middle of work. This sets up the story that follows.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Beit Hillel say:
One stands and recites, sits and recites,
reclines and recites,
walks on the road and recites,
does his work and recites.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands בית הלל's position after the verse discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, שמע may be recited in any posture or activity.

steps.title: The story: two sages switch positions at the time of שמע
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל was reclining and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was upright. When the time for שמע came, they switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who were dining in one place. רבי ישמעאל was reclining and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was sitting upright. When the time for קריאת שמע arrived, רבי אלעזר reclined and רבי ישמעאל sat up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a story. Two sages each change posture when the evening שמע arrives. This prepares the exchange between them in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר leaned over to say שמע, which matches בית שמאי's 'lie down at night'. רבי ישמעאל did the opposite and deliberately sat up. That raises the question of why he switched.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabbi Yishmael
and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
who were dining in one place,
and Rabbi Yishmael was reclining,
and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was upright.
Once the time for reciting Shema arrived,

phrases.aramaic: הִטָּה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְזָקַף רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar reclined and Rabbi Yishmael sat up.
phrases.notes: They swapped positions

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case of the positions discussed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: the two sages switch postures for שמע.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה complains with a parable about a beard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says רבי ישמעאל is like a man who grows his beard only to spite those who shave. Whatever רבי אלעזר does, רבי ישמעאל does the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to רבי ישמעאל: ישמעאל my brother, let me give you a parable. It is like a man whom people praise: 'Your beard is full!' He answers them: 'Let it be against those who destroy theirs.' You are the same. As long as I was upright, you were reclining. Now that I reclined, you sat up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges רבי ישמעאל's switch. He uses a parable to suggest that רבי ישמעאל is only being contrary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, the man keeps his beard not for its own sake but to oppose those who shave. רבי אלעזר is saying that רבי ישמעאל sat up only because רבי אלעזר leaned over, not for any real reason. This challenge calls for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: I will give you a parable
Those who destroy (shave off) their beards

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to Rabbi Yishmael:
Yishmael, my brother,

phrases.aramaic: אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה —
phrases.english: I will give you a parable: to what is this similar?
It is like one to whom people say:
'Your beard is full!'
He said to them: 'Let it be against those who destroy [their beards].'
phrases.notes: He grows it only to spite others

phrases.english: So too are you:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁאֲנִי זָקוּף — אַתָּה מוּטֶּה,
phrases.english: as long as I am upright, you are reclining;
now when I reclined, you sat up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי ישמעאל's posture switch described in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's decision to sit up for שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The switch looks like pure contrariness rather than a halachic need.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל explains: I followed בית הלל, and I was protecting the students
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that he acted according to בית הלל. He also wanted to keep the students from concluding that the halacha follows בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I acted according to בית הלל, and you acted according to בית שמאי. And more than that, maybe the students would see and fix the halacha that way for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers רבי אלעזר's complaint. His switch had a real halachic purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reclining specially for the night שמע looks like בית שמאי's rule. בית הלל allow any posture, so sitting up is fine. רבי ישמעאל sat up on purpose so the students would not think lying down is required. That would have made בית שמאי's view the accepted practice.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but furthermore
They will set the halacha for generations

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: קריאת שמע may be said in any position, standing, sitting, reclining, walking, or working. One should not act in a way that makes people think בית שמאי's stricter posture rule is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a teacher's public behavior can set halacha for students. Sometimes one must deliberately avoid a practice so that a rejected view is not mistaken for the law.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: He said to him: I acted according to the words of Beit Hillel,
and you acted according to the words of Beit Shammai.
And not only that, but
perhaps the students will see
and establish the halacha for generations.
phrases.notes: That is, according to בית שמאי

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's parable-challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל switched posture just to be contrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: He acted like בית הלל on purpose, so the students would not adopt בית שמאי's view as halacha.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha follows בית הלל: posture does not matter for קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Why did רבי ישמעאל add a second reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל needed the extra reason introduced with "ולא עוד".
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of "and not only that"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל gave a second reason, worrying about the students, on top of his first one. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's first reason was that he acted like בית הלל. But בית הלל allow reciting שמע in any position, including reclining. So why wasn't that reason enough, and why add more?

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean
And not only that / and furthermore. It adds a second reason.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "and not only that"?
phrases.notes: Refers back to רבי ישמעאל's answer in step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְלֹא עוֹד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the second half of רבי ישמעאל's answer was needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first reason (acting like בית הלל) was not enough on its own.

steps.title: Switching positions would look like following בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: Staying reclining is fine for בית הלל only if you were already reclining. Switching from upright to reclining would look like following בית שמאי and could mislead the students.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that בית הלל also allow reclining, that only applies when he was reclining from the start. But here, until now you were upright and now you are reclining. People will say: learn from this that they hold like בית שמאי. The worry is that the students will see this and fix the halacha that way for generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second reason. Lying down right when it was time for שמע would look like following בית שמאי, who require reclining at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית הלל, reclining is fine only if it is your natural position from before. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was upright, so if he lay down just for שמע, it would look like a deliberate act following בית שמאי. That is why רבי ישמעאל did the opposite and sat up: to show clearly that the halacha follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say. Introduces a possible objection.
These words apply only... Limits a rule.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think reclining is forbidden according to בית הלל. It is allowed. The problem here is only how it looks when someone changes position specifically for שמע.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ מַטִּין,
phrases.english: And if you would say: Beit Hillel also allow reclining,
that applies only where he was reclining from the start.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעַד הַשְׁתָּא הֲוֵית זָקוּף
phrases.english: But here, since until now you were upright
and now you are reclining, they will say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סְבִירָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Learn from this that they hold like Beit Shammai,
lest the students see
phrases.notes: This is the worry רבי ישמעאל mentioned.

phrases.english: and establish the halacha for generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל נָמֵי אִית לְהוּ מַטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reclining is allowed by בית הלל only when it was your original position. Switching to it for שמע looks like following בית שמאי and could mislead the students.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a sage's public actions teach halacha, so he must avoid actions that could be misread.

steps.title: Following בית שמאי still counts
steps.stepSummary: רב יחזקאל teaches that whether one acts like בית שמאי or like בית הלל, he has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יחזקאל taught: if he acted like בית שמאי, he has acted validly. If he acted like בית הלל, he has acted validly.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens: what if someone recited שמע the way בית שמאי require? רב יחזקאל says it still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the halacha follows בית הלל, רב יחזקאל holds that doing it בית שמאי's way does not cancel the מצוה. Reclining at night or standing in the morning is still a valid way of reciting שמע.

phrases.english: Rav Yechezkel taught:
If one acted like Beit Shammai, he has acted (validly);
like Beit Hillel, he has acted (validly).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי ישמעאל's story to the general question of whether following בית שמאי counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who recites שמע according to בית שמאי has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Following בית שמאי counts for nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees and says that one who acts like בית שמאי has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: if he acted like בית שמאי, he has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the opposite view from רב יחזקאל. Following בית שמאי does not count, and he must recite שמע again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, once the halacha follows בית הלל, בית שמאי's way is simply wrong and invalid. This is a direct argument with רב יחזקאל's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He has not done anything at all (the act is void)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If one acted like Beit Shammai,
he has done nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees directly with רב יחזקאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who recites שמע according to בית שמאי has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a proof from a סוכה case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites a משנה: a person with his head and most of his body in the סוכה but his table in the house. בית שמאי invalidate it and בית הלל validate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone whose head and most of his body were in the סוכה, and whose table was inside the house. בית שמאי rule it invalid, and בית הלל rule it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts bringing a proof from a משנה in סוכה. This line only sets up the case. The punchline, how בית שמאי reacted to the other side's practice, comes in steps 26–27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a debate where the two houses disagree about whether the act is valid. רב יוסף will show that in such debates, one side treats the other's practice as not fulfilling the מצוה at all. That supports his view that following the rejected opinion counts for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the proof is finished. So far it only states the case. The part that actually proves רב יוסף's point comes in the next lines of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בַּסּוּכָּה
phrases.english: As we learned: one whose head and most of his body were in the sukka
and his table was inside the house,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai invalidate, and Beit Hillel validate.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ בַּסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the source for רב יוסף's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that following the rejected opinion of בית שמאי is void.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about having one's head and most of one's body in the סוכה while the table is in the house. The proof continues next.

steps.title: בית הלל's proof from the visit to רבי יוחנן בן החורנית
steps.stepSummary: Within the quoted משנה, בית הלל bring a story: the elders of both schools found רבי יוחנן בן החורנית sitting with only his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table in the house, and nobody objected.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: There was a story where the elders of בית שמאי and the elders of בית הלל went to visit רבי יוחנן בן החורנית. They found him with his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table inside the house, and they said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: We are still inside the משנה that רב יוסף quoted. בית הלל try to prove their lenient view with a story where even the elders of בית שמאי stayed silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל argue that silence means approval. If the elders of בית שמאי saw this setup and said nothing, then even they must agree that this kind of סוכה sitting is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident used as a legal precedent
His head and the majority of his body

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
There was an incident where the elders of Beit Shammai went
along with the elders of Beit Hillel

phrases.aramaic: לְבַקֵּר אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן הַחוֹרָנִית,
phrases.english: to visit Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChoranit,
phrases.notes: This took place on סוכות.

phrases.english: they found him with his head and most of his body in the sukkah
and his table inside the house,
and they said nothing to him.
phrases.notes: Even the elders of בית שמאי did not object.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָלְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted by רב יוסף in step 25. בית הלל support their lenient ruling with a story.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's position that head and most of the body in the סוכה, with the table in the house, is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the elders visiting רבי יוחנן בן החורנית and staying silent

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the story: they told him he never fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי deny that the story proves anything. They say the elders actually told him that if this was his practice, he had never fulfilled מצות סוכה in his life. This completes רב יוסף's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Is that a proof? In fact they told him: If this is how you have been acting, you have never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה in your whole life.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's story by saying the elders did not stay silent. They clearly told him his practice was worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the line רב יוסף needed. In בית שמאי's view, someone who follows the opinion they reject has done nothing at all. Since the halacha follows בית הלל, the same logic works in reverse: someone who follows בית שמאי has also done nothing, which supports רב יוסף against רב יחזקאל.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there a proof from there? (a rejection of a proof)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is ruling like בית שמאי here. The point is only the principle: whoever follows the rejected opinion gets no credit. Since we rule like בית הלל, the one who loses credit is the person following בית שמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is how רב יוסף's proof works. It shows that acting like the rejected view is not just second-best. It counts as not doing the מצוה at all.

phrases.english: They (Beit Shammai) said to them: And is there a proof from there?!
Rather, they actually said to him:
If you have been accustomed to act this way,
you have never fulfilled the מצוה of sukkah in your life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: וּמִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית הלל's proof from the story. In doing so, it provides the key line for רב יוסף's position.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the elders' silence showed approval
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elders were not silent. They explicitly told him his practice was worthless.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: following בית שמאי makes one deserving of death
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק takes the strongest position of all: someone who acted like בית שמאי is liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Someone who acted like the words of בית שמאי deserves death.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is added to the debate. רב נחמן בר יצחק goes even further than רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have three levels. רב יחזקאל says acting like בית שמאי fulfills the מצוה‎. רב יוסף says it counts as nothing. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is so wrong that the person deserves death. His proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: עָשָׂה כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי — חַיָּיב מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One who acted according to Beit Shammai is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, more extreme opinion beyond רב יחזקאל and רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Acting like בית שמאי, against בית הלל, makes a person deserving of death.

steps.title: Proof from רבי טרפון, who risked his life to recite שמע like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his view from our משנה. רבי טרפון lay down to recite שמע like בית שמאי, put himself in danger from bandits, and the חכמים told him he deserved it for going against בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: רבי טרפון said, 'I was traveling, and I lay down to recite שמע like בית שמאי, and I put myself in danger because of bandits.' They told him: 'You deserved to pay with your life, because you went against the words of בית הלל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's strong statement. It is the story of רבי טרפון from our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger came directly from following בית שמאי's rule to lie down. While he was lying down, he was exposed to bandits. The חכמים said he deserved this danger, which shows that going against בית הלל is treated as a serious sin, not just a missed מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: I reclined / lay down on my side
You deserved to be liable with your life

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on acting like בית שמאי. רב יחזקאל says it fulfills the מצוה‎. רב יוסף says it counts as nothing, as shown by the סוכה story. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the person deserves death, as shown by the story of רבי טרפון.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Tarfon said:
I was coming along the road
and I reclined to recite Shema according to Beit Shammai
and I endangered myself because of the bandits,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדַאי הָיִיתָ לָחוּב בְּעַצְמְךָ,
phrases.english: they said to him: You deserved to be liable with your life,
because you transgressed the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the משנה source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that one who follows בית שמאי deserves death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about רבי טרפון reclining on the road and the חכמים' response to him

steps.title: New משנה: the ברכות before and after שמע, morning and evening
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. In the morning one says two ברכות before שמע and one after. In the evening one says two before and two after. One ברכה is long and one is short.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In the morning, one says two ברכות before שמע and one after it. In the evening, one says two ברכות before it and two after it. One is long and one is short.
steps.whatsHappening: The topic changes. The משנה moves from how to recite שמע to which ברכות surround it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Morning: two before (יוצר אור and אהבה רבה) and one after (אמת ויציב). Evening: two before (מעריב ערבים and אהבת עולם) and two after (אמת ואמונה and השכיבנו). The גמרא does not explicitly explain the words 'one long and one short'; the commentators do. One reading, cited by Sefaria from תוספות, is that אמת ואמונה can be said in either a long or a short version.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say which ברכה is 'long' and which is 'short,' and the commentators explain it in different ways. Do not assume an obvious meaning.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
In the morning one recites two blessings before it
and one after it.
And in the evening one recites two blessings before it
and two after it.
One long and one short.
phrases.notes: Explained by the commentators. One view (תוספות) is that the long or short version of אמת ואמונה are both valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּשַּׁחַר מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, the ברכות of קריאת שמע, after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning: two ברכות before שמע and one after. Evening: two before and two after. One is long and one is short.

steps.title: Do not change the set form of a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a general rule: the length of each ברכה, and whether it has a closing חתימה, must stay exactly as the חכמים set it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where the חכמים said to make a ברכה long, a person may not shorten it. Where they said to make it short, he may not lengthen it. Where they said to end with a closing ברכה, he may not leave it out. Where they said not to end with one, he may not add it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from step 30 continues with a firm rule. You may not change the form that the חכמים gave to the ברכות of שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said that one ברכה is long and one is short. Now the משנה says this is not a loose suggestion. Both the length and the closing line (חתימה) are fixed, and changing them in either direction is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: to end the ברכה with a closing 'ברוך אתה ה'' line (a חתימה)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לחתום does not mean 'to sign.' It means to end the ברכה with a closing line that begins 'ברוך אתה ה''.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that the wording and structure of ברכות set by the חכמים are fixed. A person cannot reshape them as he likes.

phrases.english: A place where they (the Sages) said to make it long —
he is not permitted to shorten it,
where they said to shorten it — he is not permitted to lengthen it.
phrases.notes: The words 'where they said' are understood from the first phrase.

phrases.english: where they said to conclude with a closing blessing — he is not permitted to leave it out,
where they said not to conclude — he is not permitted to conclude.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְהַאֲרִיךְ אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַצֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 30 by turning 'one long, one short' into a fixed rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The length of each ברכה, and whether it has a closing חתימה, may not be changed from what the חכמים set.

steps.title: What blessing is said first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the wording of the first ברכה before the morning שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a basic question about the content of the first morning ברכה. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה told us how many ברכות there are, but it never said what they say. The גמרא now asks for the actual wording, starting with the first ברכה of the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: the section of discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: What blessing does one recite?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's count of ברכות to asking what the first one actually says.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The wording or theme of the first ברכה before the morning שמע.

steps.title: The answer begins with רבי יעקב in the name of רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names who answers the question. רבי יעקב reports in the name of רבי אושעיא, and the content of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי אושעיא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by naming the speakers. The actual answer, a פסוק about the ברכה, comes right after this line on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a chain of quotation: רבי יעקב is passing on what he heard from his teacher רבי אושעיא. Nothing new is ruled yet. This line only opens the answer to step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So-and-so said in the name of so-and-so,' a chain of quotation
the אמורא who reports the teaching
the earlier teacher whose teaching is being reported

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
phrases.notes: The content of the statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question 'What ברכה does one say?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is attributed to רבי יעקב in the name of רבי אושעיא. Its content, based on a פסוק, follows on the next amud.
